key_insight: CatDiT is a unified diffusion-transformer framework that inversely designs heterogeneous catalysts by jointly conditioning on adsorbate, binding energy, and catalyst class to generate valid, novel structures across broad chemical spaces.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable route to property-directed catalyst discovery, improving candidate screening efficiency for reaction-specific design in heterogeneous catalysis.
method: Learns compressed latent representations of catalyst structures for efficient training and fast sampling
Supports simultaneous conditioning on discrete and continuous targets, including adsorbate type, binding energy, and catalyst class
Generates candidates spanning intermetallic alloys and oxide surfaces for inverse design
evidence_signal: For nitrogen reduction reaction design, CatDiT produced 28 DFT-relaxed alloy candidates within the target activity window and above the pure-metal *N-*H scaling line, achieving about 1.5× enrichment over the source distribution.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on a specific catalyst class and reaction setting, so generalization to broader chemistries and property targets still needs validation.
paper_title: Catalyst Diffusion Transformer: Generative Inverse Design of Heterogeneous Catalysts
